nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO4 nanorods
nodes.procedure: A 50 mL solution with 0.04 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.01 M (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O was prepared and then transferred into a 100 mL autoclave. A 2 cm × 5 cm piece of NF was transferred into the same autoclave. The autoclave was moved to a furnace for hydrothermal reaction at 150 °C for 6 h. After the reaction, the HT-NiMoO4 was successfully grown on the NF surface. The HT-NiMoO4/NF was cleaned with DI water several times and dried at 60 °C overnight under vacuum. Powdery HT-NiMoO4 was peeled from the NF surface via sonication for X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis.

nodes.name: Water bath NiMoO4 nanowires
nodes.procedure: A 20 mL solution with 0.1 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.0125 M (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O and 0.15 M urea was prepared and then transferred into a 25 mL glass vial. A 1 cm × 3 cm piece of NF was transferred into the same vial. The vial was moved to a water bath oven and maintained at 90 °C for 8 h. After the water bath reaction, the WB-NiMoO4 was successfully grown on the NF surface, and the WB-NiMoO4/NF was rinsed with DI water several times and then dried at 60 °C overnight under vacuum. Powdery WB-NiMoO4 was peeled from the NF surface via sonication for XRD analysis.

nodes.source_text: Free-standing WB-NiMoO4 nanowires were prepared based on a reported water bath (WB) method [14]... Powdery WB-NiMoO4 was peeled from the NF surface via sonication for XRD analysis.

nodes.name: Hierarchical HW-NiMoO4 synthesis
nodes.procedure: The preparation of hierarchical interconnected HW-NiMoO4 was based on a rational combination of the aforementioned hydrothermal and water bath (HW) methods. First, the HT-NiMoO4/NF was prepared via the hydrothermal method described above. Subsequently, 1.5 cm × 2.5 cm pieces of HT-NiMoO4/NF were placed into vials with the solution as described above for the water bath method (0.1 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.0125 M (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O and 0.15 M urea). For the water bath reaction, the temperature was set at 90 °C while the time was 2 h for HW-NiMoO4-2h. Powdery HW-NiMoO4-2h was peeled from the NF surface via sonication for XRD analysis.

nodes.name: Thermal nitridation
nodes.procedure: The same nitridation process was employed to convert all the different NiMoO4 samples described above into NiMoN. Specifically, each sample was transferred into a tube furnace with a flowing gas of 120 sccm NH3 and 30 sccm Ar. The thermal nitridation was conducted at 400 °C for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.203 nm for Ni(111) nanodots on nanowires and 0.246 nm for Ni0.2Mo0.8N(100) in nanowire bulk.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1c, d shows high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of HW-NiMoN-2h.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern displays diffraction rings of Ni(200), Ni(111), Ni0.2Mo0.8N(110), and Ni0.2Mo0.8N(100).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern for HW-NiMoN-2h displayed in Fig. 1e shows the diffraction rings of Ni (200), Ni (111), Ni0.2Mo0.8N (110), and Ni0.2Mo0.8N (100).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS point analysis shows Ni:Mo ratio ≈1:1; mappings confirm uniform distribution of Ni, Mo, and N throughout nanowires and nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping shown in Fig. 1f–h and the EDS linear scan shown in Fig. S5 suggest the uniform distribution of Ni, Mo, and N throughout the nanowires and nanorods of HW-NiMoN-2h.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Ni 28.35 wt% and Mo 41.65 wt%, giving atomic ratio Ni:Mo ≈1.1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES was further conducted to determine the amounts of individual metals in HW-NiMoN-2h. As shown in Table S1, the weight percentages of Ni and Mo were found to be 28.35% and 41.65%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of HW-NiMoN-2h shows peaks of Ni0.2Mo0.8N(100), Ni(111), Ni(200), Ni(220); HT-NiMoN shows additional MoO3(021) peak indicating incomplete nitridation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b shows the XRD patterns for HT-NiMoN, HW-NiMoN-2h, and WB-NiMoN, indicating that... its XRD pattern exhibits four peaks of Ni0.2Mo0.8N (100), Ni (111), Ni (200), and Ni (220).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni0 (853.2, 870.5 eV), Ni2+ (856.0, 873.9 eV), Mo3+ (229.6, 232.7 eV), Mo4+ (230.4, 235.3 eV), N 1s metal-N (397.3 eV), indicating Ni metal and Ni0.2Mo0.8N with surface oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra were obtained to investigate the valence states of elements in HW-NiMoN-2h... The XPS measurements thus suggest that HW-NiMoN-2h is mainly composed of Ni metal and Ni0.2Mo0.8N.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measurements at various scan rates used to determine double layer capacitance (Cdl) values; HW-NiMoN-2h exhibits highest Cdl and thus highest ECSA among NiMoN samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical surface area (ECSA) analysis was employed to characterize the active area of selected NiMoN samples electrochemically [41]. Based on the CV measurements in Fig. S7, the Δ(j) of each sample was plotted as a function of the scan rate and their double layer capacitance (Cdl) values were calculated, as shown and listed, respectively, in Fig. 3b.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area highest for HW-NiMoN-2h among NiMoN samples.
